headline: Hearts, four days after 7-1, face in-form Trabzonspor
summary: Trabzonspor beat Beşiktaş 2-0 on Sunday, their fourth win in a row, and Hearts arrive in Trabzon after losing 7-1 at Celtic. Mohamed Salah already has eight league goals, and although striker Paul Onuachu is out injured, the market sees no contest: across 10 bookmakers, with the margin removed, Trabzonspor are 73.5% to win. The handicap has moved from 1.48 to 1.67 goals in their favour, yet the goals line sits at 3.32 — so the result looks settled and the scoreline does not.
read: Trabzonspor arrive on four straight wins, with Salah on eight goals and a 2-0 derby win behind them, and the market has them at 73.5% to win, rated about 1.7 goals the better side. Hearts come four days after a 7-1 defeat at Celtic, short in midfield, and the goals line of 3.32 suggests the game will be open even though the result is not in much doubt.

facts.fact: Trabzonspor have won their last four matches, scoring 13 goals and conceding two, including a 2-0 derby win over Beşiktaş on Sunday.
facts.meaning: They arrive on the best run of the two teams and with a place in the Conference League phase already up and running after a 4-2 win at KuPS.

facts.fact: Hearts were beaten 7-1 at Celtic on Sunday, their heaviest defeat of the run and a fourth game without a win in five.
facts.meaning: They travel to Turkey four days after shipping seven, with one win in their last five in all competitions.

facts.fact: Mohamed Salah has eight goals in the opening eight Süper Lig rounds and scored again in the 2-0 win over Beşiktaş.
facts.meaning: He is the obvious focal point of the Trabzonspor attack, and one a Championship-level defence has to survive for 90 minutes.

facts.fact: Trabzonspor's win chance has risen from 69.0% to 73.5% in the last two days, with the draw down to 15.1% and Hearts at 11.4%.
facts.meaning: The market rates a home win as roughly six times more likely than a Hearts win before kick-off.

facts.fact: The handicap fair line has moved from -1.48 to -1.67, with the main line now Trabzonspor -1.75.
facts.meaning: The market now rates Trabzonspor about 1.7 goals better than Hearts and still makes the -1.75 line close to a coin flip (48.2%).

facts.fact: Manager Thomas Reis has ruled striker Paul Onuachu out of the Hearts match with the injury he picked up against KuPS.
facts.meaning: Trabzonspor lose a centre-forward option on the day they are rated 1.7 goals stronger, so the goals may have to come from Salah and the wide players.

facts.fact: The goals fair line sits at 3.32, with over 3.25 priced at 51.6% — just on the over side of three goals.
facts.meaning: The market expects an open game, more likely than not to pass three goals, despite the mismatch on the result.

facts.fact: Trabzonspor sit 3rd of 36 in the Conference League phase on three points; Hearts are 19th on one after their 1-1 home draw with Nordsjaelland.
facts.meaning: It is a chance for Trabzonspor to put themselves in the qualifying places and for Hearts to avoid a second straight European defeat.

sources.fact: Trabzonspor have won four games in a row, scoring 13 goals and conceding two, and are aiming for a fifth straight win when they host Hearts.
Trabzonspor manager Thomas Reis has ruled out striker Paul Onuachu for the Conference League match against Hearts due to an injury sustained against KuPS.
Thomas Reis took charge of Trabzonspor's final training session at the Mehmet Ali Yilmaz Facilities in Trabzon on October 21 ahead of the Hearts match.
Mohamed Salah scored as Trabzonspor beat fierce rivals Beşiktaş 2-0 in the Süper Lig, taking his tally to eight goals in the opening eight rounds.
Trabzonspor defender Stefan Savic said his team can up the gears even more against Hearts after downing fierce rivals Beşiktaş.
Trabzonspor beat Finland's KuPS 4-2 in their Conference League opener.
Hearts were humiliated 7-1 by Celtic at Celtic Park in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday.
Hearts are short on options in midfield for Thursday's Conference League tie against Trabzonspor in Turkey.
